title: PowerPoint for Windows: create a presentation with Copilot from PowerPoint Home
notes: claim 49: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the Cloud Policy route mixes selecting an existing configuration with the creation wizard and omits the Create step needed for that route. The claim that Microsoft Learn does not describe starting presentations from PowerPoint's opening or File menus is also incorrect; the default, rollout notice, licence-assignment command and registry setting are supported.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy route is Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote:
On the Policy configurations page, select Create.

On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups

On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.
claims.fix: Use the documented creation route: 'Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content'. The current route substitutes selecting an existing configuration for Create; the cited page documents Choose the scope and Configure Settings in the creation wizard. The privacy-controls page already cited supplies the policy name.

claims.claim: Setting usercontentdisabled to DWORD 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables the analyze-content policy.
claims.quote:
Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled  2=Disabled

[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]
"usercontentdisabled"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: The analyze-content policy controls the category of connected experiences, not only Copilot.
claims.quote: These are experiences that use your Office content to provide you with design recommendations, editing suggestions, data insights, and similar features. For example, PowerPoint Designer or Translator.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is Microsoft's recommended role for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.claim: Licence assignment is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page.
Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to.
In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps.
Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence to the user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.

Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: At least License Administrator or User Administrator is required for licence assignment.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.quote:
